info.description:
Tempy Hub Backend — care-home SaaS API.
Import only this collection (variables live on the collection).
Base: {{url}} = http://localhost:6060/api/v1/
Accounts are created by an administrator; there is no public signup.
Run App → Auth → Login to save token into collection variables.
Note: communications/* email helpers and send-notification are not mounted in commonRoutes by default.
Auth: POST auth/login and GET auth/me return the same `access` block (memberships, modules, moduleMenu, moduleAccess, organizations). `/auth/me` also returns `user`, `staffProfile`, and `hasDirectReports`.

item.name: Family Invitations
item.description: Invitations to join a family, and the ones the next of kin sent.

request.description: A signed-in user accepts an invitation addressed to their email. No password; used to link an existing account to another resident.

Invite Family: the next of kin invites a relative. Body: residentId, name, email, relationship (a value from relationship options). The invitee gets an email with a one-time link valid for 7 days. With EMAIL_ENABLED on the sender never receives the link. While it is off, nothing is delivered, so the response also includes acceptUrl and this request saves its token in familyInviteToken for accept family invitation. Next of kin only (403 otherwise); 400 for a missing name or bad relationship or email; 409 if the email belongs to a staff member, is already a member, or already has a pending invitation. Figma screen: Invite Family (Send Invite).
Invitations this next of kin sent for the resident, newest first, with status (pending, accepted, revoked, expired). Optional query: status, page, limit. Next of kin only.

item.name: Family Members
item.description: Residents, members, family code, join requests and handover.

request.description: Options for the Relationship dropdowns (Grandson, Daughter, Niece...). Needs a family token but no active link, so the Join A Family screen can use it. Figma screens: Join A Family, Invite Family.

Residents the member is actively linked to, with the active one flagged (Who are you viewing?). residentId is optional: the resident the app is showing; without it the first one is flagged. Residents of a home with Family Engagement off are left out. Returns an empty list when the member has no active link yet. Built as one aggregation (links joined to organization, resident and home). Figma screen: Home Family Tab (Who are you viewing? and the header dropdown).

My Family: the people linked to the resident, with name, photo, relationship, Next Of Kin badge, status and isYou. The next of kin also sees people who asked to join (status pending, canReview true); everyone else sees active members only. canRemove and canReview say which buttons to show. Figma screen: My Family.

Removes an active member; their access ends on their next request. Only the resident's next of kin. 409 for the next of kin (hand over first) or for someone who hasn't been approved (reject the request instead); 404 for anyone else's member. Figma screen: My Family (Remove). Notification: Removed from family goes to that member; nothing is sent when they remove themselves.

Leave this family. Body: residentId. The next of kin gets 409 next_of_kin_must_hand_over until someone has taken over. Leaving also withdraws any handover that was asked of this member. Figma screen: Profile & Settings (Leave This Family).

The resident's current family code and when it expires. code is null when there is none or it has expired, so the app shows Make A New Code. Next of kin only: 403 for another family member, 404 when the resident isn't one of yours, 400 when residentId is missing. Figma screen: Invite Family (family code card).
Make A New Code: creates a code valid for 14 days and voids the old one. The code never contains the resident's room number. Next of kin only. Figma screen: Invite Family (Make A New Code).

The Code Accepted card: checks a typed code and returns the home name only (the resident stays hidden until approval). Wrong 404, expired or replaced 410, and 429 after 5 wrong tries in 15 minutes (the message says how many minutes are left). Figma screen: Join A Family (code entry, Wrong, Expired, Locked).

Send Join Request: body code and relationship (one of the values from relationship options). Creates a pending request for the next of kin or the home to approve. Errors: 400 invalid_relationship, 404/410/429 for the code, 409 join_request_pending (one at a time), 409 family_link_exists, 409 email_used_by_staff. Figma screen: Join A Family. Notification: New join request goes to the resident's next of kin and the site's site and line managers.
The member's pending request (home name, Waiting), or null when there is none. Figma screen: Join A Family (Request Sent, Waiting).

PUT with body {"action":"cancel"}. Cancel Request, after the confirmation dialog. Only the member who asked, and only while it is pending (409 otherwise, 404 for anyone else's request). Figma screen: Join A Family (Cancel Request).
Requests waiting for review, oldest first, paginated. Next of kin only (403 for another member, 404 when the resident isn't yours, 400 without residentId). Figma screen: My Family (Review).

PUT with body {"action":"approve"}. Approves a pending request: the person becomes an active member and sees the resident from their next call. Only the resident's next of kin; 404 for anyone else (so other families' requests stay hidden), 409 if the request was already decided. Figma screen: My Family (Review). Notification: Request approved goes to the person who asked.

PUT with body {"action":"reject"}. Rejects a pending request. The person can send a new request later. Only the resident's next of kin; 404 for anyone else, 409 if already decided. Figma screen: My Family (Review). Notification: Request declined goes to the person who asked.

Who the next of kin can hand over to: active members (canSelect true) and people still waiting for approval (shown, canSelect false), plus the option to let the home choose. Next of kin only. Figma screen: Leave Margaret's Family (Handover To).

Asks one member to take over as next of kin. Body: residentId and toMemberId (a memberId from handover candidates). The next of kin keeps the role until the person accepts. Errors: 400 handover_target_required / handover_to_self, 404 family_member_not_found, 409 handover_member_not_approved or handover_pending (one open handover per resident). Figma screen: Leave Margaret's Family (Ask James To Take Over).

Lets the home choose the new next of kin. Body: residentId and homeChooses true. The next of kin keeps the role until the home assigns someone. Figma screen: Leave Margaret's Family (Let Florence House Choose).

The open handover the caller is part of, or null. direction is outgoing for the next of kin who asked and incoming for the person asked; to is null when the home chooses. residentId is optional. Figma screen: Leave Margaret's Family (James Must Accept).

PUT with body {"action":"accept"}. The person asked accepts and becomes next of kin; the previous next of kin stays a regular member. Done together or not at all. 404 for anyone but the person asked, 409 if no longer open or no longer valid (the next of kin changed or someone left).
PUT with body {"action":"decline"}. The person asked declines; the next of kin keeps the role. 404 for anyone but the person asked, 409 if no longer open.

PUT with body {"action":"cancel"}. Keep My Role: the next of kin withdraws the request. 404 for anyone but the next of kin who asked, 409 if no longer open. Figma screen: Leave Margaret's Family (Keep My Role).

item.name: Moderation
item.description: A family member's own uploads, from photo to approval.

request.description: New Upload: Upload Photos. Body is form-data with one image in the field file (choose a file in Postman). Images only, up to 10 MB; the server checks it is a real image, resizes it to 2048px and stores it. Sets mediaId for send upload for approval. One photo per call.

New Upload: Upload Photos, several at once. Form-data field files; select up to 10 images in that one row (10 MB each, 50 MB together). Every file is checked before any is stored, so one bad file stores nothing and the error names it. Returns photos, a list of mediaId in the order sent. Sets mediaId (the first) and mediaIds (all, as a JSON list): in send upload for approval replace ["{{mediaId}}"] with {{mediaIds}} to attach them all.

New Upload: Send For Approval. Body: residentId, message (up to 500 characters), mediaIds (up to 10, from upload photo), includeInGazette, clientId. Needs a message or a photo. 400 photos_cannot_be_shared when the resident has photo sharing off (a message alone is allowed); 400 for too many photos, a message over 500 characters or photos that are not yours; 404 for a resident you are not linked to. The same clientId returns the upload already made. Saved as pending; nobody but you sees it until a manager approves. Notification: New upload to review goes to the site's site and line managers.

query.description: Tab: pending, approved or rejected
One resident

request.description: My Uploads: Approved, Waiting For Approval and Not Approved (with rejectionReason). Optional query: status (pending, approved, rejected), residentId, page, limit. meta.counts has the three totals and ignores the status filter. Photos show the blurred copy once one exists. Rejected uploads disappear 30 days after rejection.

My Uploads: Edit And Resend. Body (all optional): message, mediaIds, includeInGazette. A pending or not approved upload returns to pending with the reason cleared. 409 upload_not_editable once approved; 404 for someone else's upload or after you were removed from the family. Notification: New upload to review goes to the site's site and line managers when a Not Approved upload is sent again.

My Uploads: delete my own upload. Only a pending or not approved upload can be deleted; an approved one is already shared with the family and is final (409 upload_not_deletable). Its photos are deleted with it, including the files in storage, and so are the notifications about it, so the managers' New upload to review disappears. 404 upload_not_found for an upload that is not mine, for a resident I am no longer linked to, or one that is already gone. Returns uploadId. Family token.

item.name: Gazette
item.description: The gazette being collected, the printed ones and the reader.

request.description: The Gazette tab's top card: the gazette being collected now. Query: residentId (required). scheduled is false until the organization has saved a gazette schedule (then issue is null and there is nothing to show). Otherwise issue has number (No. 15), state (collecting, or notStarted before the first issue begins), periodStart, periodEnd, periodLabel (15 Oct – 28 Oct 2026) and closesAt (the Closes 28 Oct pill). messageCap is 30, messagesUsed is the 9 in '9 of 30 messages' (approved messages meant for the gazette; at most the cap), messagesSent is how many were sent in all, remaining, overflow (sent beyond the cap, which wait for the next gazette), isFull (the Gazette full screen) and percentFull for the progress bar. A message printed in an earlier gazette, or taken out by staff, does not count again.

Printed gazettes: the gazettes the home has printed for the resident, newest first. Query: residentId (required), page, limit. Each row has gazetteId, title (The Hughes Family Gazette), issueNumber (Gazette no. 14), periodLabel (1 Oct – 14 Oct 2026), messageCount, pageCount (the 6 pages), printedAt and givenAt (the 'Printed 15 Oct · given 15 Oct' line, with givenAt empty until the home records it) and latest, true on the newest one overall (the Latest pill and the card on the Gazette tab). Only printed gazettes are listed.

Read gazette: the printed gazette for the reader. gazetteId comes from printed gazettes. title, issueNumber, periodLabel (No. 14 · 1–14 Oct 2026), residentName (for Margaret), homeName, pageCount, printedAt and givenAt. cover is the best photo of the issue (the newest photo) with its message, headline, authorName and relationshipLabel, or null when there is no photo. messages are the family's messages oldest first: authorName, relationshipLabel (Daughter), message, photos and sentAt. life is Life at the home: title, text, photoUrl and postedAt. Photos are the blurred copy wherever one exists. Anything no longer allowed is left out on every read: a resident whose photo sharing is off has no photos, and a wall post that was removed is gone. 404 gazette_not_found for a gazette that is not printed, belongs to another resident, or is not yours.

Returns greeting (Good morning, Sarah: by the time of day at the resident's home), homeName, resident (the one shown), residents (the header dropdown, with isActive), nextVisit (the Your Next Visit card, null when there is none), visiting {paused, reason, since}, gazette (the Gazette Due card: scheduled, issue, remaining), notices (banners: visitingPaused when the home has paused visiting; joinRequests, with a count, for a next of kin who has requests to review) and unread {notifications, messages} for the badges. item.name: Visits
item.description: My Visits, Book A Visit and the Visit Pass.

request.description: My Visits. Query: residentId (required), tab (upcoming or past; 400 invalid_visit_tab for anything else), page, limit (default 20, max 50). Upcoming is soonest first, past is newest first and includes declined and cancelled ones. A row is either my own request or an invitation From The Home (fromTheHome true): id, source (family or home), status (requested, confirmed, declined, cancelled; for an invitation invited until I answer, then going or cantMakeIt), startAt, endAt, partySize, note, decisionNote (the home's reply to a request), canCancel (my request, not yet over), canReply (an invitation I can still answer) and hasPass (Visit Pass available). meta.counts has the two tab totals; meta.visiting.paused, reason and since drive the Visiting is paused notice. A request is only visible to the person who made it; invitations from the home are visible to the whole family of the resident.
Home Family Tab, Your Next Visit: the soonest visit that is confirmed, or an invitation I said I would attend. visit is null when there is none. visiting is the same paused notice as My Visits.

Book A Visit: what the home offers. days (the next few days, date and weekday; today is left out once no time remains), visitingHours {start, end}, protectedTimes [{start, end, label}], maxPartySize, timezone and the visiting notice. The app builds the time to pick itself, from the visiting hours, a start every half hour; the server checks the time it sends. The home sets these per site; until it does, the defaults are visiting hours of 12:00 to 18:00, 14 days ahead and up to 6 people. Sets visitDate and visitTime (the opening time) for the request below.

Book A Visit, the Request button. Body: residentId, date (YYYY-MM-DD from visit options), time (HH:mm on the half hour, inside the visiting hours with at least half an hour before closing, and not in a protected time), totalPeople (1 to maxPartySize) and an optional note (up to 500 characters). The visit runs from that time until the visiting hours end. It is a request until the home confirms it. Errors: 403 visiting_paused, 400 invalid_visit_time for a time that isn't offered, 400 visit_protected_time for a closed time, 400 for a date or number that isn't offered or a day that has passed, 409 visit_already_requested for the same time, 429 once five requests are waiting. Notification: New visit request goes to the site's site and line managers.

PUT with body {"action":"cancel"}. My Visits, Cancel Request: cancels my own request while it is waiting or confirmed and not over; a confirmed visit also stops its kiosk code working. 409 visit_not_cancellable otherwise, 404 for anyone else's visit. Notification: Visit cancelled by family goes to the site's site and line managers.

PUT with body {"action":"going"} (I'll Be There) or {"action":"cantMakeIt"} (Can't Make It). Answers an invitation From The Home for myself only; each family member answers separately and may change their mind until the visit is over. Going gives me my own kiosk code for the Visit Pass; Can't Make It withdraws it. 409 visit_not_replyable once the visit is over or cancelled, 404 for a request or another family's visit. Notification: Invitation accepted or Can't make the visit goes to the site's site and line managers when the answer changes; repeating the same answer notifies nobody.

Visit Pass. visit is my next confirmed visit (or an invitation I said I would attend) and code is its kiosk code, the same 6-digit invitation code the kiosk already accepts: show it as the QR code. Both are null when there is no such visit. guests are the people without the app and carRegistration the car, as saved below. The code does not refresh by itself yet: a code that changes every few seconds needs the kiosk to check it.

Saves the guests without the app and the car registration for this resident. Body: residentId, guests (up to 10 names, each up to 60 characters), carRegistration (up to 12 letters, digits, spaces or hyphens; send an empty string to clear it). Anything left out stays as it was. Returns the pass.

This endpoint allows you to send an email to the specified recipients.

#### Request Body

- title (string, optional): The title of the email.
    
- emails (array of strings): The list of email addresses to which the email will be sent.

- body (string, required): The body content of the email.
    
- config (object):
    
    - fromEmail (string, required): The sender's email address.

query.description: url returns a signed link to the stored PDF (valid 5 minutes) as { url, expiresAt, filename } instead of the file; a PDF that is drawn on demand is still returned as the file

request.description: The Preview and the Download PDF button. Returns the newsletter as an A4 PDF drawn like the home's template: header, welcome, the month's posts with photos, coming up and notices side by side, new residents, photo gallery and footer. Only the sections that are switched on are drawn. A draft is drawn fresh, leaving out posts removed and residents whose photo sharing is off since it was built; a sent newsletter serves the copy stored when it was sent (when the PDF channel was on). Query download=true sends it as an attachment, otherwise it opens inline. In Postman use Send and Download to save it. Needs familyEngagement.view.

Newsletters: pick the month (the Newsletter month dropdown). Body: branchId (an owner or super admin must pick the site; a site or line manager uses their own), month (2026-10), and optionally title and template (classic, the only one for now). One newsletter per site and month (409 newsletter_exists_for_month); remove the draft to start again. The draft is filled in: highlights from the month's live wall posts, gallery from their photos, new residents admitted that month with photo sharing on, the footer from the site, the standard Share your photos notice, and who signs it (your name and role, such as Claire Adams, Site Manager). The response is the whole builder: the sections with their switches, the preview content (the home, organizationName, periodLabel and issueNumber for the Issue 14 line), counts for each section, and recipients {families, members} for the 42 families badge. Needs familyEngagement.manage. Needs the Family Engagement module (404 when it is off) and the matching permission: familyEngagement.view to read, .manage to change, .approve to decide join requests. Owners and super admins always have them; a site or line manager needs them granted.

Save draft (and every edit on the builder). Only a draft. Body, all optional: title, template, sections (welcome, highlights, comingUp, notices, newResidents, gallery as true or false), welcome {text, signedBy}, highlights [{postId, title, text, mediaId}], comingUp [{date, time (14:30), title, description, category}] (kept in date order), notices [{title, body}], newResidentIds [residentId], gallery [{mediaId, caption}], footer {homeName, address, phone, email}, delivery {inApp, email, pdf} (the choices under Send & Delivery), refill (a list of sections to pull from the wall again: highlights, gallery, newResidents; use it after new wall posts were added, it replaces only the named sections and a list sent in the same request wins). A list sent replaces the whole list; anything not sent is left alone. Highlights must be live posts of the site, gallery photos must come from them, and new residents must be admitted residents of the site with photo sharing on. 409 once scheduled or sent. Needs familyEngagement.manage. Needs the Family Engagement module (404 when it is off) and the matching permission: familyEngagement.view to read, .manage to change, .approve to decide join requests. Owners and super admins always have them; a site or line manager needs them granted.

Send & Delivery: the Send newsletter button (When: Send now). Body: action send, and optionally delivery {inApp, email, pdf} to set the checkboxes now; without it the choices saved on the draft are used and at least one must be on (400 newsletter_delivery_required). A newsletter needs at least one switched-on section with something in it (400 newsletter_empty). Channels: inApp notifies every active family member at the site once each; pdf draws the PDF and stores it (pdfKey); email sends each distinct family address its own message (nobody sees another address) with the PDF attached. The email is sent only when EMAIL_ENABLED is true on the server; otherwise the channel is recorded as skipped. deliveryLog says what happened per channel: done with count (and failed), failed, or skipped. A failing address does not stop the others. Sending is done before the response returns, so a very large home takes longer. Posts removed, or residents whose photo sharing was switched off, since the draft are left out. The response is the sent newsletter with status sent, sentAt, sentBy, sentTo {families, members} and deliveryLog. One send wins if it is clicked twice (409 newsletter_already_sent for the other). Both use the requirement schema: an assigned requirement is met when its latest record has not expired, and staff are the active ones. supervisionAppraisal: compliantPercent (meetings done against meetings due so far, supervisions and appraisals together, using each staff member's own interval and start date), supervisions {pending (booked or due within 30 days), overdue (staff behind)} and appraisals {dueThisMonth, overdue}. openShifts: the five soonest upcoming open shifts {siteName, startsAt, endsAt, urgentCover}.

request.description: The Super Admin dashboard in one call. Platform admin only (Admin Login, no x-org-id): anyone else gets 403. Query: year (the year of the two charts, the current year by default; 400 invalid_statistics_year outside 2000 to 2100) and organizationId (the Select organization dropdown of Organizational Overview; the organization with the most modules by default; 404 organization_not_found). summary (the cards, over every organization): organizations, sites (branches), pendingInvitations (staff and owner invitations that are still pending and not expired), professionals (professional people records), siteAndLineManagers (active site and line manager memberships), staff (active staff profiles), residents (admitted) and totalMonthlyRevenueGbp (the Total Monthly Revenue card). onboardingGrowth (Onboarding Growth): year, months (Jan to Dec), organizations and sites (running totals at the end of each month; null for months still to come) and changePercent, the growth of organizations plus sites against a year ago (null when there were none then). topOrganizations (Top Organizations, five at most, most modules first): organizationId, name, status and modules (enabled modules that have not expired); organizations lists them all for the dropdown. revenueByOrganization (Revenue by Organization): organizationId, name and monthlyRevenueGbp for every organization. organizationOverview (the bars for the selected organization, null when there are none): organizationId, name, sites, staff, residents, modules, siteManagers and lineManagers. dataUsage (Data Usage & Images Shared): year, usedGb, planQuotaGb (the one plan limit times the number of organizations, null until the limit is set), quotaPercent, images and files {gb, percentOfUsed} and months, one per month with imagesGb, filesGb and totalGb. A past month shows what the nightly measurement recorded on its last run that month, so months before recording began are null; the current month shows today's numbers. Blank for now: totalMonthlyRevenueGbp and every monthlyRevenueGbp are null, because nothing stores revenue yet; the frontend shows them empty. Not included: Sites by Region, because nothing stores a branch's region.

item.name: All Settings
item.description: Billing, family and visit settings in one call.

query.description: The site for visits (an owner, super admin or platform admin picks one)

request.description: All the settings in one call: billing {planLimitGb, baseTierGbp, overageGbpPerGb}, family {configured, gazette {issueEveryDays, messageCap, anchorDate}, updatedAt} and visits (the visiting rules of one site: branchId, timezone, visitingHours {start, end}, protectedTimes, daysAhead, maxPartySize, paused, pausedReason, pausedAt). access says which sections the caller may use: billing is for a platform admin only; family is for an owner or super admin of the organization; visits is for an owner, super admin, site manager, line manager or staff member who holds familyEngagement.view (an owner or super admin needs no stored permission). A section the caller may not use is left out, and so are family and visits when the Family Engagement module is off or no x-org-id is sent. A platform admin sends x-org-id only to also get family and visits. Query branchId picks the site for visits: an owner, super admin or platform admin must send it, and visits is null until they do; a site manager, line manager or staff member always gets their own site.

Saves any of the three sections in one call. Send only the sections you want to change, and inside a section only what changes. billing {planLimitGb (a number above 0 up to 1000000, or null to clear it), baseTierGbp and overageGbpPerGb (0 to 100000)}: platform admin only; it changes the one limit and prices every organization shares (400 invalid_plan_limit, invalid_billing_price or invalid_billing_settings). family {gazette {issueEveryDays 1-90, messageCap 1-100, anchorDate YYYY-MM-DD}}: owner or super admin; it changes the organization in x-org-id, and the first save needs anchorDate and switches the gazette schedule on. visits {branchId, visitingHours {start, end} (HH:mm, at least half an hour apart), protectedTimes [{start, end, label}], daysAhead 1-60, maxPartySize 1-20, paused, pausedReason}: needs familyEngagement.manage; it changes one site (400 invalid_visit_settings), and pausing cancels the visits still to come and tells the families. Every section is checked for access first and nothing is saved if any is refused (403 insufficient_role). Then the sections are saved in the order billing, family, visits, so a section that fails validation (400) stops the rest: sections before it are already saved. Returns the saved sections. 400 nothing_to_update when no section is sent, 400 invalid_settings_section when one is not an object.

Billing & Usage settings, sent as the billing section of the all settings call. Platform admin only (403 insufficient_role for anyone else); an x-org-id is not needed. They are the one plan limit every organization shares and the prices on the Billing Readiness card. planLimitGb is a number above 0 up to 1000000, or null to clear it (400 invalid_plan_limit); baseTierGbp and overageGbpPerGb are numbers from 0 to 100000 (400 invalid_billing_price). Send only what changes; a billing section with none of the three is 400 invalid_billing_settings. Returns all three values. Read them with all settings.

item.description: Storage used by each organization against one shared plan limit. Everyone sees the screen: a platform admin every organization, an owner their organization and its branches, a site manager, line manager or staff member their own branch. The pencil edits the organization (update organization, in the Organizations folder); only a platform admin changes the billing settings.

query.description: Platform admin only: one organization (the Filter by Organization dropdown)
Organization name, owner name or owner email
usedDesc (default), usedAsc, percentDesc or name

request.description: The Billing & Usage screen in one call. Any signed-in role may call it: Super Admin (platform admin), owner, site manager, line manager or staff. Who sees what: a Super Admin (platform admin, Admin Login, no x-org-id) gets one row per active organization, and passes organizationId (clicking an organization, or the Filter by Organization dropdown) to get that organization's branches the way its owner sees them: one row per branch, the cards of that organization and the organization itself in meta.organization. An owner (or an organization's super admin) sends x-org-id and gets one row per branch of their organization, with their organization itself in meta.organization. A site manager, line manager or staff member sends x-org-id and gets only their own branch. Query: organizationId (platform admin only: the Filter by Organization dropdown), keyword (organization name, owner name or owner email for a platform admin; branch name or owner name or email for the others), sort (usedDesc is the default, usedAsc, percentDesc or name), page, limit (default 10). data has one row per organization for a platform admin: organizationId, name, owner {name, email}, usedGb, planLimitGb (the same for every organization; null until the platform admin sets it), usagePercent, status (normal below 60%, moderate from 60%, high from 90%, overPlan above 100%, noLimit when no limit is set) with statusLabel, images {gb, percentOfUsed, count}, files {gb, percentOfUsed, count} (PDFs, documents and records), emergencyNotifyOffsite, measuredAt, measuring, unmeasured and canEdit. A branch row (owner, site manager, line manager, staff) has branchId, organizationId, name, owner {name, email} (the organization's owner), usedGb, planLimitGb (the organization's limit, shared by its branches), usagePercent (the branch's share of that limit) with status and statusLabel, images, files, measuredAt, unmeasured and canEdit (always false). The pencil opens Edit Organization: show it on an organization row when canEdit is true (a platform admin, an owner or a super admin) and fill the dialog from the row (name, owner name and email, which cannot be changed, and emergencyNotifyOffsite); Save Changes is update organization (PUT /admin/organizations/:organizationId with name and settings.emergencyNotifyOffsite). meta.summary is the four cards for everything in scope, ignoring the search (all organizations for a platform admin, the organization for an owner, the one branch for a site manager, line manager or staff member): activeOrganizations, totalUsedGb with quotaPercent (used against planLimitGb for each organization, which is totalPlanGb), planLimitGb, images {gb, percentOfTotal, count}, files {gb, percentOfTotal, count} and billing {status withinPlan or overPlan, label, organizationsOver, overageGb, overageChargeGbp, baseTierGbp, overageGbpPerGb}. A platform admin also gets meta.organizations for the dropdown. GB here are 1024 x 1024 x 1024 bytes. Usage is measured from the storage bucket every night, so measuredAt says how fresh it is.

query.description: One branch of the organization: its own usage detail

request.description: The usage detail page of one organization (click a row on the Billing & Usage table). The id in the path is organizationId. Only a Super Admin (platform admin, no x-org-id) or the owner or super admin of that organization (send x-org-id with the same id) can open it; a site manager, line manager or staff member gets 403 insufficient_role, and an owner asking for another organization gets 404 organization_not_found. organization: organizationId, name, owner {name, email} and status. storage (the Storage Usage card): totalUsedGb, planQuotaGb (the one limit every organization shares, null until it is set), quotaPercent, status with statusLabel, images {gb, count, percentOfTotal} and files {gb, count, percentOfTotal} (PDFs, documents and records), measuredAt and unmeasured. categories (the Category Breakdown card): one entry each for residents (Resident Photos & Media), staff (Staff Profile Photos), floorPlans (PEEP & Floor Plans), documents (Documents, Signatures & Leave Attachments), family (Family Photos, Newsletters & Gazettes), visitors (Visitor Photos & Signatures) and profiles (Profile Pictures), each with label, gb, percentOfUsed, images {gb, count} and files {gb, count}; they add up to totalUsedGb. Show images.count for a photo category and files.count for a document category. branches (Sites & Operating Branches): one per branch, biggest first, with usedGb, images {gb, count} and files {gb, count}. billing (Billing & Pricing): planLimitGb, monthlyBaseGbp, overageGbpPerGb, status (withinPlan or overPlan) with label, overageGb and projectedOverageGbp (overageGb times the overage price). record: createdAt and updatedAt of the organization. GB are 1024 x 1024 x 1024 bytes, rounded to four decimals (4.5 MB is 0.0044 GB). The figures are the last nightly measurement, so a new organization shows 0 until it is first measured, which happens when the server starts. Add the query branchId to get the usage detail of one branch of that organization instead (click a branch row on the organization's branch list). A branch detail has scope {type: branch, branchId}, organization {organizationId, name, owner {name, email}, status}, branch {branchId, name, status} and the same storage, categories, billing and record sections for that branch only; planQuotaGb is the organization's shared limit, and branches is just that one. A branch that is not in the organization is 404 branch_not_found. The branch's category figures are filled by the next measurement after a restart or the nightly run; until then every category shows 0.

item.name: Conversation/Messages
item.description: Messages from the home to next of kin, one way. Use a family token to read them and a staff token (site manager, line manager, owner) to send.

query.description: inbox (default), favorite or archived; 400 invalid_chat_tab for anything else

request.description: FAMILY token (Login Family). Messages from the home, one thread per home, newest first. Only active next of kin see anything; anyone else gets an empty list. Each row has conversationId, chatName (the home's name), chatState, unreadCount, canMessage (always false: families cannot reply, so hide the composer) and lastMessage (messageContent, senderName, createdAt). meta.unread is the unread total for the badge. Live updates: connect to the /chat socket with auth {token} (the same login token) and listen for receiveMessage; the room is taken from the token, and the socket cannot send anything. Sets conversationId.

FAMILY token. The messages in one thread, newest first: _id, senderName, messageContent, createdAt and isRead (as it was when the thread was opened). Opening the first page marks the whole thread read and clears unreadCount, which the home sees in its sent list. 404 conversation_not_found for anyone else's thread, or once the person is no longer next of kin.

FAMILY token. PUT with body {"action":"favorite"}: action is default (back to the inbox), favorite or archived; 400 invalid_chat_action for anything else. It only changes how this person sees the thread.

STAFF token (Login Staff or Login line Manager). A message from the home to next of kin; they read it in the app and cannot reply. Body: audience (all: every active next of kin at the site; selected: the next of kin of residentIds, one to 100 residents of that site; people: the next of kin in recipientIds, one to 200 people from recipients), message (plain text, up to 2000 characters) and branchId (a site or line manager uses their own site; an owner or super admin must send it, or get 400 branch_required). Only active next of kin are reached, each person once even when they are next of kin of several chosen residents; carers and family members who are not next of kin are not. Each person has one thread per home, gets an in-app notification and a live push. Returns broadcastId, sentAt, recipients, conversationId (set when exactly one person got it), residentsWithoutNextOfKin and recipientsNotReached (people who are not next of kin at this site); 400 message_no_recipients when nobody could be reached, 404 resident_not_found for a resident of another site, 403 outside_managed_branch for another site. Sets broadcastId. Needs familyEngagement.manage; rate limited. Needs the Family Engagement module (404 when it is off) and the matching permission: familyEngagement.view to read, .manage to change, .approve to decide join requests. Owners and super admins always have them; a site or line manager needs them granted.
